Latin word

dēlectō

dēlectō, dēlectāre, dēlectāvī, dēlectātum

verb, first conjugation: the thing enjoyed is the subject (mē dēlectat), or the passive dēlector takes the ablative · Conjugation on Wiktionary

delight; in the passive, enjoy; delight, please

In this lexicon

  • enjoy

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Sen. 51: quibus ego incrēdibiliter dēlector; Cic. Att. 2.6.1: aut librīs mē dēlectō; Aug. Conf. 1.9.15: sed dēlectābat lūdere

  • pleasure

    also used · classical · Traupman 302

Examples

  • veniō nunc ad voluptātēs agricolārum, quibus ego incrēdibiliter dēlector

    I come now to the pleasures of farmers, which I enjoy beyond beliefCic. Sen. 51

    In the entry for enjoy

  • sed dēlectābat lūdere

    but what we enjoyed was playingAug. Conf. 1.9.15

    In the entry for enjoy

  • oblectā tē cum Cicerōne nostrō quam bellissimē

    have as lovely a time as you can with our little CiceroCic. Q. fr. 2.11.4

    In the entry for enjoy

  • Sed etiam mē dēlectat basipilā lūdere.

    But I also like to play baseball.Traupman 42

    In the entry for enjoy

  • sē oblectāre

    to amuse oneselfTraupman 271

    In the entry for enjoy

  • capere laetitiam ex (+ abl.)

    to take pleasure inTraupman 389
